summary: All 49 full occurrence records were reviewed. Romance, family alliance, liking a house/food/proposition, willingness, beloved states and mercy were distinguished by Turoyo construction and context.

Preterit rḥəmli/rḥimoli/rḥəmlax has an L-series experiencer and can express an ongoing state or current wish. The reviewed evidence contains no bare qaṭəl Preterit counterexample: roḥəm/roḥam/ruḥmi are Infectum forms, including culinary and generic preference clauses.

I.1 affective love/liking takes unmarked nominal stimuli, object suffixes, reciprocal ḥḏoḏe, or an evaluated proposition. I.2 willingness takes bare or d-linked action complements and can also take a nominal desired pen type or prospective kinship. It is not a noun-versus-clause split.

Fronted ḥlime and Raqiqe in JTM 2.10/1 may be object-related predicates or abbreviated alternatives; ḥliṯo in JTM 2.9/3 likewise needs native-speaker checking. The source's Thymian for kəzbarto in JTM 2.7/9 is retained only as an editorial question.

Detransitive Part. Pass. marks being loved/dear/popular, with copular past markers -wa/-wayne, ʕal lebi/ʕal community experiencers and s Aloho as the lover. These do not entail a completed change to being loved.

III mercy has the merciful person or God as subject and ʕal- target, including contracted appe/aʕle. New III Infectum-wa and Imperativ are secure from full contexts and the parallel sǝm raḥme. No light-verb sense is manufactured from that parallel; no standalone səm occurrence is assigned here.

The family alliance formula is explicitly metalinguistically explained in JTM 1.3/5 and recorded as one idiom. Arabic la yərḥəm abuk is a fixed curse, whereas the liturgical Syriac titles at 94/42 remain quotations and do not establish Turoyo II.
məstarḥamme at JTM 3.1/31 is retained as unresolved evidence, not a certified III Detransitive sense. Its mutual agreement context cannot by itself determine the morphological template.

The inherited Nomen actionis box contains an -ono property/agent adjective. Because the glossary's terminology can be idiosyncratic, no automatic relabeling to Part act. is made from the reader's claim. mraḥmono at 116/36 is filed provisionally alongside that inherited family.

PrS 4/1 duplicates the inherited reciprocal-love example cited prs 10/10; reconcile editions/numbering before changing that citation. 24/319 is already present and needs no duplicate or false missing-example correction.
Determine the root, template and argument coding of məstarḥamme b ḥḏoḏe at JTM 3.1/31; is it an integrated reciprocal form, a contact form or a different derivation? No new stem/sense was published.
Are mraḥmono and raḥem at 94/42 exclusively quoted Syriac hymn language? More independent Turoyo evidence is required before adding II.

Should native marḥmono/mraḥmono in III be kept in the inherited Nomen actionis category, treated as a lexical agent/property noun, or assigned a form category on morphological grounds? The reader's Part act. label is not assumed.
Confirm ko-Preterit krəḥamme in PrS 43/60 against a contracted Infectum reading.
At JTM 2.10/1 are ḥlime/Raqiqe secondary predicates or topical substantivized alternatives? At JTM 2.9/3 what is the referent/gender of ḥliṯo?
The edition renders kəzbarto as Thymian in JTM 2.7/9. Verify the plant without replacing the source translation.
Reconcile PrS 4/1 with inherited prs 10/10. The same sentence is not a second independent attestation.
Check whether the Arabic curse is productive in Turoyo beyond quotation; the single code-switched form does not establish a new I mercy sense.
